title: MCP Agent Fine tuning Workshop - Ronan McGovern
talk_summary: A workshop showing how to run an MCP tool-using agent, log full multi-turn traces (tools + messages + reasoning), curate them manually, and LoRA fine-tune a small Qwen model on those traces. The core transferable idea is trace capture, curation, and unrolling as a data pipeline, not the fine-tuning itself.

takeaways.what_they_do: Every agent run logs two parts: the full tool list and the complete multi-turn message history including parsed reasoning, saved to disk for later training/eval use.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we need to know a list of the tools and we need the full conversation history

takeaways.technique: Unroll multi-turn traces into multiple training/eval rows
takeaways.what_they_do: A 3-turn trace becomes 3 rows (full, first-2, first-1), giving 3x data from one run and matching how chat templates only inject the latest reasoning.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we want to unroll that into three rows ... we get kind of three for the price of one

takeaways.technique: Manual trace curation before trusting data
takeaways.what_they_do: Speaker edits bad traces by hand (deleting a user turn, merging turns, or asking a stronger model to rewrite) and discards noisy runs rather than training on them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: There's always going to be noise, so some of the traces won't be good ... just manually adjust the trace

takeaways.technique: System prompt as scaffolding, excluded from training data
takeaways.what_they_do: They inject an explicit system prompt telling the model exactly which tools to call to get a clean trace, then drop that prompt from the training data so the model learns the behavior natively.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you get it to create a nice tidy trace and then you don't have to include the system prompt in your training data

takeaways.what_they_do: They cap exposed tools: ~25-50 for open-source models, up to ~200 for Claude, because too many tools confuse the model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: For open source models, probably you don't want more than maybe 25 to 50 tools. I think for claude, you can probably handle 200

takeaways.technique: Naive truncation of tool responses (and its known limit)
takeaways.what_they_do: They truncate long tool outputs (e.g. browser accessibility trees) to the top portion to fit context, acknowledging the model then can't see the whole page.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I'm just naively truncating it ... the LLM won't probably be able to see the full length of the page
